def-standard-orientation-of-the-affine-s: The ordered edge basis defines a simplex orientation and fixes the alternating face signs, including the positive zero-simplex convention; neither formula characterizes an iff condition.
def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-sin: The chart pullback integral defines a number for each smooth simplex, with a separate degree-zero convention; no property is characterized by two opposing implications.
lem-simplex-integrals-are-independent-of: The claim is invariance under orientation-preserving affine coordinates and under neighbourhood extension, not a criterion for when two integrals agree.
lem-stokes-theorem-for-the-standard-simp: The displayed equality is the signed boundary formula for an already given smooth form on a standard simplex; it is not a hypothesis-conclusion equivalence.
thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-c: For given smooth chains and forms, the asserted integral equality follows by finite linearity and simplex Stokes; its reverse is not a separately stated theorem.
lem-the-de-rham-complex-and-pullback-ext: This extends exterior differentiation and pullback to locally extendible boundary forms and proves algebraic identities; no condition is claimed necessary and sufficient.
def-de-rham-integration-cochain-map: The assignment sends each differential form to its evaluations on smooth simplices, with a zero map in negative degrees; it defines a map rather than an iff criterion.
thm-de-rham-integration-is-a-cochain-map: The single cochain-map identity equates coboundary after integration with integration after differentiation on every form; the statement has no reverse implication.
thm-the-de-rham-map-on-cohomology-is-wel: The assertion constructs a linear map on cohomology classes from the cochain map; it does not characterize which forms or classes admit such a map.
prop-naturality-of-the-de-rham-map: Both displayed equations are naturality identities for the given smooth map, on cochains and classes respectively; neither is an iff test for smoothness.
lem-the-de-rham-homotopy-formula-extends: Given a smooth homotopy with endpoint extensions, the operator defined by time integration satisfies the displayed chain-homotopy identity; no converse is asserted.
lem-the-de-rham-map-is-an-isomorphism-on: Convexity of the supplied coordinate domain is a sufficient setting for the computed cohomology and isomorphism, not a necessary condition for that isomorphism.
lem-de-rham-mayer-vietoris-with-boundary: The short exact sequence and its connector are constructed for an ordered two-open cover using a partition lift; the statement gives no necessary-and-sufficient test for a cover.
lem-the-de-rham-and-smooth-singular-maye: The two equations check compatibility of restriction and difference maps with integration; they are identities, not converse criteria for commutative diagrams.
lem-the-de-rham-map-commutes-with-mayer-: The claim is the connector-intertwining equation for the fixed two-open-cover sign conventions; neither direction of a biconditional is stated.
thm-the-de-rham-map-is-an-isomorphism-on: The theorem gives the piecewise-isomorphism assumptions as sufficient for the union via Mayer-Vietoris; it does not claim they are necessary.
thm-de-rham-theorem-for-smooth-singular-: Integration is asserted to be a natural vector-space isomorphism for every manifold in the stated class; the class is not characterized by the existence of an isomorphism.
cor-de-rham-vector-space-comparison-with: The map composed from smooth integration and inverse restriction is proved a natural isomorphism; no reverse hypothesis about manifolds is claimed.
lem-affine-diagonal-and-front-back-shuff: This constructs finite affine chains connecting the diagonal and signed shuffle by a boundary identity; it states no necessary-and-sufficient condition.
lem-integration-over-the-signed-shuffle-: The case distinction concerns form-degree pairs in a signed-shuffle integral formula; it is a value computation, not a logical equivalence.
lem-de-rham-integration-respects-wedge-a: The explicit operator K gives a cochain-homotopy equation and hence product compatibility for closed forms; no converse criterion for closedness is asserted.
thm-de-rham-theorem: The theorem asserts that the constructed comparison is a natural unital graded-algebra isomorphism under its hypotheses; it does not characterize those hypotheses.
cor-de-rham-cohomology-depends-only-on-t: Homotopy equivalence supplies a cohomology isomorphism, with homeomorphism as a special case; the reverse implication is not claimed.
rem-ring-form-of-the-de-rham-theorem-nee: This remark distinguishes linear bijectivity from multiplicativity and identifies the wedge-cup homotopy needed for the ring result; it is not biconditional.
def-compactly-supported-de-rham-cochain-: The compact-support spaces, differential, and quotient define a cochain complex and its cohomology; the displayed quotient is a definition, not two implication directions.
prop-proper-smooth-maps-pull-back-compac: Properness is used as a sufficient hypothesis for compact support of pullbacks, while the support containment holds for every smooth map; necessity is not asserted.
prop-compactly-supported-de-rham-cohomol: The proposition constructs contravariant pullback and verifies composition and identity for proper smooth maps; it does not say only such maps can act.
lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-ch: Finite chart localization defines an integral, proves choice independence, and proves compact Stokes; none of these equalities characterizes compact support by an iff.
thm-integration-descends-to-compactly-su: Vanishing on exact top forms makes finite-localization integration descend to the quotient, including dimension zero; no converse criterion is stated.
lem-zero-integral-compactly-supported-to: Zero integral is stated as a sufficient condition for a compactly supported primitive, with a separate dimension-zero case; the lemma does not state the converse.
lem-compactly-supported-top-cohomology-p: Overlapping oriented coordinate balls with normalized bump forms give equal top cohomology classes; equality is not claimed to force overlap.
cor-top-de-rham-cohomology-of-a-closed-c: For a nonempty closed connected oriented manifold, integration is asserted an isomorphism with the reals; the hypotheses are not characterized as necessary.
lem-degree-is-well-defined-and-independe: The degree scalar is shown unique and independent of the normalized form, yielding the universal integral equation; this restates one value rather than asserting an iff test.
def-local-orientation-sign-of-a-regular-: The sign records whether the derivative's determinant-line map preserves the chosen orientation ray, with separate dimension-zero convention; this is a definition, not an iff proof obligation.
thm-regular-value-formula-for-compact-su: For a supplied regular value, degree equals the finite sum of local signs; the displayed formula is not claimed to characterize regular values.
lem-smooth-orientation-sign-is-the-local: The local homology multiplier agrees with the smooth determinant-line sign under fixed generator conventions; equality of signs is not an iff criterion for smoothness.
thm-regular-value-formula-for-degree: The formula computes degree from signed regular preimages and, for closed manifolds, identifies homological degree; no reverse regularity criterion is asserted.
